blocks: A black key takes its sharp spelling, written as the letter, a hyphen and the word sharp: Music/Note/4/C-sharp. The page body gives the flat spelling the same way, as D-flat-4. The page name, the file name Music___Note___4___C-sharp.md and the site URL Music/Note/4/C-sharp/ all read the same, which My/Principle/Referential-Transparency asks of a name. A # would be percent-encoded as %23 on disk and in the URL, and would start a tag in body text.
The lowest octave is -1. MIDI note 0 is Music/Note/-1/C.

Every instance takes its note name as its alias::: the letter and octave for a white key, so [[G8]] links Music/Note/8/G, and the letter, -sharp- and the octave for a black key, so [[C-sharp-4]] links Music/Note/4/C-sharp. In octave -1 the minus sign is spelled out as minus: [[C-minus-1]] and [[C-sharp-minus-1]], and Live's octave -2 is C-minus-2.
Names from Ableton Live and Arturia

Ableton/Live and Arturia's MicroFreak manual name MIDI note 60 C3, so their octave numbers run one lower. Add one to their octave number before linking a note: a drum pad Live labels D#2 is D-sharp-3. Write their names in the same style on a note page: D-sharp-2.
